name: Cinderbull
body:
Cinderbull
CR 9

This giant, red bull has dragon’s wings and snorts fire out of its snout. Its hooves leave scorch marks on the ground and its very presence seems to boil the air around it.

XP 6,400
N Large magical beast (fire)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +16; Aura (5 ft., 1d6 fire)

DEFENSE

AC 22, touch 9, flat-footed 22 (+13 natural, –1 size)
hp 126 (11d10+66)
Fort +13, Ref +7, Will +7
DR 5/magic; Immune fire
Weaknesses vulnerability to cold

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor)
Melee gore +19 (3d8+8/19-20 plus 1d6 fire), 2 hooves +13 (1d8+4 plus 1d6 fire)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks breath weapon (30-ft. cone, 10d6 fire damage, Reflex DC 21 for half, usable every 1d4 rounds), trample (3d8+16, DC 23)

STATISTICS

Str 26, Dex 11, Con 23, Int 2, Wis 15, Cha 10
Base Atk +11; CMB +16; CMD 26
Feats Cleave, Improved Initiative, Improved Critical (gore), Iron Will, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (gore)
Skills Perception +16

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Heat (Su)

A cinderbull generates heat so intense that anything touching its body takes 8d6 points of fire damage. Creatures striking a cinderbull with natural attacks or unarmed strikes are subject to this damage, but creatures striking with melee weapons are not. The heat can melt or burn weapons; any weapon that strikes a cinderbull is allowed a DC 21 Fortitude save to avoid damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm hills and plains
Organization solitary, pair, pack (3–4), or herd (5–12)
Treasure none

Cinderbulls are formidable creatures found in the areas with extremely high volcanic activity. They most often lair on the volcanos themselves, preferably the active ones, and hunt their prey on the plains of rock and ash around them. While cinderbulls are omnivores and can subside on shrub and grass if they have to, they strongly prefer to devour meat, either raw or thoroughly roasted with their flames beforehand. As fierce and temperamental as any bull, cinderbulls are both larger and far more dangerous than common cattle. Their skin is tough enough to stop blades, and their dragonlike wings can carry their enormous bulk through the air with limited, but still surprising, agility. While their fire affinity might not be readily apparent judging by their appearance alone, a quick inspection will confirm that the creatures are at least as married to this element as red dragons. They huff smoke and fire out of their snouts, it being their preferred weapon for both hunting and more serious combat. A cinderbull’s body is almost as hot as the molten rock they lair beside, and its heat is intense enough to burn creatures standing even a few feet back with superheated air. Beings that have the misfortune of actually touching the cinderbull feel the true intensity of this heat, with horrified predators often finding their paw fast aflame and burnt to a crisp after trying to slash a cinderbull with their claws. Even keeping the creature at bay with weapons is hardly possible, as even the slightest contact with the bull’s skin may result in the blades melting and wooden shafts turning into ash.

Cinderbulls live in herds but are not pack hunters, and most individual members of the herd set out daily by themselves to satiate their own hunger through hunting or grazing, sharing only with a less successful mate or own calves. They mostly keep to their territories and rarely go on destructive rampages, thus making their eradication a low priority for nearby communities. Races immune or highly resistant to fire, like fire giants or azers and salamanders stranded outside of their own plane, sometimes domesticate these creatures and use them as beasts of burden, mounts or even train them for war. Despite their name, cinderbulls aren’t exclusively male and instead are similar to any other cattle. Their milk, when cooled down, is highly nutritious, though quite taxing on the stomach. While races capable of domesticating cinderbulls are seldom known as traders, both the milk itself and cheeses produced from it are held in high regard by dwarves and other hardy races, who admire their nourishing properties, full taste and extremely long shelf life. Same does not necessarily go for their meat, as its fireproof properties make it nearly impossible to cook. While this heavily limits ways in which cinderbull meat can be prepared, it excels as steak tartare and dried jerky.

An average cindebull is close to 8 feet tall at the withers and 16 feet in length, with a horn span of almost 7 feet itself and a weight of almost 2 tons. Some males grow considerably larger, greatest of them suitable as mounts for even fire giants. This enormous, apelike beast has shaggy fur and a vicious underbite. Its arms end with three claws, two of them as large and sharp as any greatsword. The creature lets out an earth-shaking roar and pounds its massive chest, ready for combat.
